title: Rahul Gandhi acquitted in 2018 defamation case over remarks on Amit Shah
content: A special MP/MLA court in Sultanpur dismissed a defamation case against Congress MP Rahul Gandhi on Monday. This case originated in 2018 due to remarks Gandhi made about Amit Shah during a rally. Vijay Mishra, a local BJP politician, filed the complaint alleging Gandhi's comments were defamatory. Rahul Gandhi appeared before the court in 2023, where he secured bail successfully.

title: E100 cars get regulatory green light today ahead of planned launches
content: The government has amended the Central Motor Vehicles Rules to facilitate the registration of flex-fuel vehicles capable of running on 85% to 100% ethanol blended petrol. As car manufacturers gear up to introduce their E100 models soon, this initiative promises to lessen emissions and curb reliance on crude oil imports. Notably, existing vehicle owners are not required to make any modifications.

title: 'Insult to India itself': Rajnath Singh attacks Kharge over 'baap' remark against PM Modi
content: Defence minister Rajnath Singh has taken a strong stand against Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's statements about Prime Minister Modi, labeling them as disrespectful to both the leader and the nation. Singh asserted that Modi remains focused on serving citizens and undeterred by such comments. Following these remarks, a protest by the BJP's Patna Metropolitan unit was promptly organized.

title: 99 runs leaked in 2 T20Is! Bhuvneshwar Kumar gets a message from Morne Morkel
content: Bhuvneshwar Kumar's comeback has not gone as planned. The 36-year-old conceded 49 runs in the first T20I against New Zealand and 50 in the second, taking just one wicket across the two matches. His economy rate of 12.37 has been the highest among India's bowlers in the series.

title: Crocodile meat bite in Thailand lands Ujjain official in hot water
content: Rajkumar Rathore, an officer of the Ujjain Municipal Corporation, was seen in a viral video sampling crocodile meat. The clip, reportedly shared by his wife, sparked controversy regarding his foreign travel. Rathore traveled to Thailand without obtaining the necessary permission for his trip. The Ujjain Municipal Corporation is now reviewing the situation for any potential rule violations.

title: Peter Thiel renews Apple criticism: ‘Nothing new after Steve Jobs’
content: During a recent podcast interview, billionaire investor Peter Thiel vocalized his discontent with Apple, underscoring a perceived lack of innovation since the departure of Steve Jobs in 2011. Thiel noted that, although Apple continues to enhance its existing lineup, there has been no introduction of groundbreaking technologies. He also pointed out the mounting competition Apple faces in the realm of artificial intelligence.

title: Rs 1L penalty on Shangri-La for service charge
content: The Central Consumer Protection Authority has fined Shangri-La Eros hotel in New Delhi for an illegal service charge. The hotel had automatically added a 10% service charge to bills, which was considered unfair. After receiving a consumer complaint, the CCPA directed the hotel to stop this practice immediately. The hotel argued that the service charge was discretionary and optional.

title: Indian woman, 25, turns Ireland deportation notice into comedy routine
content: An Indian woman who moved to Ireland in 2022 to study at Trinity College Dublin is now using her real deportation notice in stand-up comedy performances. Jaishree Malik, 25, lost her job after delays in extending her immigration permission left her unable to work. Despite receiving further job offers, she could not resolve her visa status and now plans to return to India voluntarily on November 14.

title: Vande Bharat sleeper services on Mumbai-Bengaluru, Delhi-Varanasi routes in next one week
content: Railways will introduce two Vande Bharat sleeper train services on Mumbai-Bengaluru and Delhi-Varanasi shortly. The Mumbai-Bengaluru service is expected to be inaugurated on October 31. Meanwhile, the Delhi-Varanasi service is scheduled for November 1. These routes will enhance overnight travel options for business and pilgrimage purposes. The Mumbai-Bengaluru route will cover the journey in approximately 15 to 16 hours.

title: Yellow alert for 2 Andhra districts today, red alert on Oct 27-28 amid Cyclone Arnab
content: The India Meteorological Department has issued a red alert for extremely heavy rainfall on October 27. Several districts including Kakinada and East Godavari are expected to experience this severe weather. An orange alert has been announced for other districts, indicating heavy to very heavy rainfall. Yellow warnings for heavy rainfall have been issued for additional areas like Palnadu and Prakasam.

title: Gukesh vs Sindarov: What do world's top GMs think about the match?
content: With less than a month remaining for the World Championship match in Geneva, D Gukesh faces a confident Javokhir Sindarov, who tore through the Candidates Tournament in Cyprus. While Gukesh has struggled to rediscover his peak form, the world's top grandmasters believe the unique format of match play could change the dynamics. From psychological pressure and opening preparation to experience and momentum, the 14-game duel promises a real battle of minds.

title: Minnesota court reverses reopening of 300-acre farm estate over 1989 will
content: In a significant Minnesota inheritance case, the state Court of Appeals has reinstated a 2017 ruling concerning the estate of farmer Clarence Vatthauer. Disputes arose from conflicting wills dated 1982 and 1989, leading to a previous court's decision being vacated. The appeals court's ruling underscored the necessity of procedural compliance and the need for finality in estate administration, reshaping the understanding of inheritance law.

title: Samsung told to refund Rs 98,000 with 9% interest over Z Flip6 screen failure
content: In a recent ruling by a consumer commission in Haryana, Vicky Kapoor emerged victorious in his case against Samsung concerning his defective Samsung Z Flip6. The company was ordered to reimburse Kapoor Rs 88,000 following identified service gaps tied to warranty shortcomings. Just after purchase, the phone showcased severe issues, which Samsung disputed by placing blame on alleged physical damages, but the commission found their evidence lacking.

title: Google CEO Sundar Pichai admits that cloud business is forgoing short-term revenues
content: In a strategic pivot, Google has prioritized its computing resources for Artificial Intelligence (AI) research, even as the demand for its cloud services surges. CEO Sundar Pichai acknowledged that this focus could hinder short-term cloud revenue, as powerful AI models consume substantial computational capacity, limiting access for commercial clients. To maintain its edge in AI advancements, Google plans to invest significantly in AI and cloud infrastructure moving forward.

title: Why children carry the same toy from room to room, according to psychology
content: Transitional objects play a crucial role in children's emotional development, serving as sources of comfort during times of stress and change. Items like soft toys or blankets become important companions that help young ones navigate feelings of separation and insecurity. Studies illustrate how children gravitate toward familiar possessions, enhancing their sense of safety.

title: Actress arrested over Rs 5 crore extortion from ex-BJP MLA’s daughter
content: Urmila Sanawar was arrested by police in Haridwar after allegations of extortion surfaced. The complaints involved demands for Rs 5 crore and property transfer from Suresh Rathore's daughter. Sanawar allegedly made threats to kill family members if her demands were not met. Additionally, she is accused of making derogatory remarks about Rathore online. This incident occurs amidst ongoing CBI investigations into related audio recordings.

title: EC refuses to give details of SIR software, cites ‘trade secrets, IPR'
content: Election Commission of India declined to share the name of the software used for identifying electoral roll errors. The request for information was made under the Right to Information Act. A social activist from Telangana sought details about the software and algorithms used in the process. The Commission stated that no new software was developed for the exercise conducted.

title: After 2 decades, Jamia Millia Islamia announces resumption of student union elections
content: Jamia Millia Islamia has ordered the holding of students' union elections within 15 days after constitutional approval. The university revoked disciplinary actions taken against students during recent protests and issued an inquiry into security conduct. Protesting students will publicly apologize for statements made against the administration and remove related social media posts. Classes will be conducted online amid the current tensions on campus.

title: Beyoncé's childhood Houston home sold in May 2026 after $1.275m listing
content: Beyonce's childhood home in Houston, Texas, found a buyer after being listed for $1.275 million in April 2026. Her family purchased the 1935 property in 1987 and lived there until 1994. The 4,010-square-foot house has undergone extensive renovations, including upgrades to its kitchen, bedrooms and outdoor spaces. Its connection to the singer attracted multiple offers and interest from fans across the United States.

title: Giacometti chandelier bought for £250 later sold for £2.922m in 2023
content: A chandelier created by Alberto Giacometti sold for £2.922 million at a Christie's auction in February 2023. Originally purchased for £250 by British artist John Craxton in the 1960s, it remained in his family until his death. The chandelier was commissioned by art patron Peter Watson for the literary magazine Horizon, which published many famous authors. It underwent extensive authentication process before its auction, confirming its historical significance.

title: Kansas court rejects neighbours' claim to 5.13 acres behind 65-year-old fence
content: A property dispute in Kansas involved two landowners contesting a 65-year-old fence’s ownership claims. The court upheld that legal property boundaries in deeds are more valid than physical markers like fences. Neighbours Dan Hittle and the Loftuses presented conflicting arguments regarding the ownership of 5.13 acres. The Loftuses' adverse possession claim was rejected due to insufficient evidence of an agreed boundary.

title: Mecca country officials to hold joint meeting in Tehran; discuss regional security
content: Senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey are set to visit Tehran for a joint meeting. This will be the first high-level contact since the renewed Houthi conflict escalated. The meeting aims to discuss regional security, drawing on Iran's experience with national security. Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure have increased, prompting military responses from the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen.

title: Devdutt Padikkal's 199, Washington Sundar's fifty put India A in control
content: India A made impressive strides on Day 3 of their unofficial Test match against New Zealand A. Devdutt Padikkal led the charge with an impressive score of 199, setting the team at a formidable 488 for 8. Washington Sundar's unbeaten 51 strategically positioned the team for a possible declaration due to looming rain. The second innings will present New Zealand A with a significant uphill battle.

title: 'Utilizing Iran for politics': IDF chief, Netanyahu clash over military action
content: Tension brews within Israel's leadership as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and IDF chief Eyal Zamir disagree on possible military action against Iran. This clash before elections raises eyebrows about political motives behind military strategies. Netanyahu highlights the imminent threat Iran poses and urges immediate action during Trump's administration. As the election approaches, Netanyahu faces tight competition from Gadi Eisenkot, suggesting possible political deadlock with no clear majority in view.

title: Walking in Delhi, Mumbai or Bengaluru? Here’s what nobody tells you
content: Walking in major Indian cities such as Delhi, Mumbai, and Bengaluru presents numerous challenges for pedestrians. Broken footpaths and unsafe crossings discourage individuals from walking, leading to increased traffic and pollution. The unique issues faced by each city contribute to the decline in walking as a mode of transport. Effective solutions involve creating uninterrupted footpaths and prioritizing pedestrian needs during urban planning.

title: Just one run short! Devdutt Padikkal falls for 199; reaction to umpire goes viral
content: Devdutt Padikkal fell one run short of a double century during the first unofficial Test match. He was dismissed for 199 runs after an appealed catch decision by the umpire. Padikkal's innings helped India A recover from an early collapse in their second innings. India A had been bowled out for 113 runs in their first innings. His contribution was significant despite the disappointing nature of his dismissal.

title: IND vs NZ: Big blow! Ishan Kishan ruled out, BCCI shares update
content: India had also brought in uncapped wicketkeeper-batter Kumar Kushagra as cover for the injured Kishan. The BCCI has confirmed that Kushagra will remain with the squad for the third match. India have won the first two matches and lead the five-match series 2-0. The third T20I will be played in Wellington on October 27.

title: 'Had enough': Thousands protest in Prague against Czech govt's media funding overhaul
content: Thousands gathered in Prague to protest government proposals affecting public television and radio funding. The planned changes would replace licence fees with state budget allocations, raising concerns about media independence. Critics argue that these measures may expose broadcasters to political pressure and reduce their financial stability. Public media employees announced plans for a strike on November 3, with a larger rally scheduled for November 15.

title: BJP files police complaint against Kharge over 'baap' remark targeting PM Modi
content: Bharatiya Janata Party has lodged a police complaint against Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge in Patna. The complaint relates to Kharge's remarks about Prime Minister Modi during an event during 139th birth anniversary Bihar's first CM, Shrikrishna Singh. Krishna Kumar Singh, a BJP worker, demands an apology from Kharge within 24 hours. The initial report was filed at Kotwali police station, then transferred to Gandhi Maidan.

title: What happened in 5 seconds? Newlywed enters hotel room, collapses at door before death
content: Muskan Simolia collapsed and died shortly after checking into a hotel with her husband Nilesh. Her father has accused Nilesh of murder following her unexpected collapse near the hotel room's entrance. CCTV footage shows the moments leading to her fall but does not clarify the cause of her collapse. Investigators are examining the circumstances surrounding her death and have detained her husband for questioning.

title: Saudi Arabia’s Singapore plan: How Riyadh aims to protect Asian oil supplies from 2027
content: Saudi Arabia is set to store crude oil in Singapore starting in the second half of 2027. This arrangement aims to enhance energy security in the region amid supply disruptions. Singapore's Jurong Rock Caverns will provide storage facilities for Saudi crude oil supplies. The agreement will allow Saudi Aramco to bring supplies closer to key Asian markets.

title: Bank holiday on Valmiki Jayanti: Will banks remain shut on October 26? Check list
content: As October unfolds, India's vibrant festival season translates into various state-specific bank holidays. On October 26, banking services will pause in Tripura, Chandigarh, Jammu and Kashmir, and Himachal Pradesh. Important dates approaching include Karva Chauth on October 29 and Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's birth anniversary on October 31. Although digital transactions persist, customers are encouraged to verify local holiday observances to sidestep any unexpected closures at physical branches.

title: '15-20 rounds fired': 2 killed, 2 injured as assailants open fire outside homes in Punjab
content: Two individuals have died and two others are hospitalized following gunfire in Angadpura locality. Authorities identified the deceased as Sahil Jindal and Gagan Jindal, who were cousins. Witnesses report at least 15-20 rounds were fired by assailants from a Black Scorpio SUV. Police have initiated an investigation and recovered three shells from the scene. Families of the victims have named suspects, suggesting personal enmity may be involved.

title: Can an unmarried daughter claim maintenance from her father? Bombay high court answers
content: The Bombay high court has upheld a family court's order for a father to pay maintenance to his children. The father challenged the maintenance order, arguing his children were no longer entitled to payment. The court ruled his son was a minor when the original order was made, and his daughter's need for support was valid.

title: Man killed as Mercedes driven by judge’s minor son hits scooter in Keralam
content: A 17-year-old boy collided with a scooter, resulting in the death of a 55-year-old man on Container Road. The deceased, Jayabalakrishnan, was returning home after closing his roadside eatery when the accident occurred. Initial investigations revealed that the minor was alone in the car and had not consumed alcohol. Police have registered a case which will likely involve additional charges of culpable homicide.

title: ‘Brazil is no one’s backyard’: Lula’s swipe at US after Bolsonaro’s defeat
content: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has won a closely contested runoff election against Flávio Bolsonaro in Brazil. Lula's victory confirms left-wing leadership in Brazil and strengthens it in Latin America. He emphasized the need for public participation in governance while addressing supporters. Bolsonaro, in contrast, sought closer ties with the Trump administration and called for election result annulment.

title: All Haryana cities breached annual PM10 limit every year since 2019
content: Haryana's cities have not met the annual PM10 air quality standard set by the government since 2019. Monitoring data indicates that all cities exceeded the annual limit, raising concerns about systemic pollution issues. Varied readings from each city show steep fluctuations in PM10 levels over the years. The National Clean Air Programme needs to include more cities across Haryana to address pollution comprehensively.

title: Over 10 lakh NCR vehicles won't be able to enter Delhi from November 1
content: Delhi plans to prohibit entry of vehicles not meeting BS6 emission standards in NCR from November 2026. Over 10 lakh vehicles in Gurgaon, Faridabad, Noida, Greater Noida, and Ghaziabad may be affected. Gurgaon and Faridabad hold around 2 lakh vehicles below BS6 standards, mostly consisting of BS3 and BS4 categories. Additionally, approximately 50,000 commercial vehicles in both locations do not comply with the new regulations.

title: 'What did I do wrong?': How being dropped from India team pushed ex-star into depression
content: Amit Mishra faced significant challenges after being excluded from the Indian cricket team for an extended period. He battled depression for 18 months, questioning his performance while continuing to play. A conversation with a selector helped him realize he needed to improve his domestic performance to succeed. After reflecting on his situation, he managed to return to the Indian team in 2008.

title: Delhi Police register case over Jamia Campus trespassing, defacement
content: Hundreds of students and alumni have gathered at Jamia Millia Islamia for the 14th day of protests. They are demanding the restoration of student union elections despite university classes being moved online. The university has closed its gates and libraries, while police have increased their presence around campus. The situation escalated as police registered a case following unauthorized entry by individuals associated with the protest.

title: In the 1880s, Colorado's Lulu City boomed on silver, then became a ghost town

title: Thick smoke emanates from North Block; six fire tenders on site
content:
NEW DELHI: Thick smoke was seen billowing from the Union secretariat's North Block here on Monday, prompting authorities to rush six fire tenders to the spot, an official said. A police officer said some repair work was underway at the building, which might have led to a minor fire. No casualty has been reported so far. Delhi Fire Services received a call at 11.10 am reporting smoke emanating from the building, following which six fire tenders were dispatched, the official said.
